writer.markdown:
## Company overview

Costco Wholesale Corporation operates membership warehouses across the United States, Puerto Rico, Canada, Mexico, Japan, the United Kingdom, Korea, Australia, Taiwan, China, Spain, France, Iceland, New Zealand, and Sweden. Its merchandise spans sundries, dry groceries, deli, liquor and tobacco, along with non-food categories such as appliances, small electronics, hardware, sporting goods, tires and apparel. It sits in the Discount Stores industry within the Consumer Defensive sector and has a market capitalisation of $408.09B. The shares trade at $920.65, within a 52-week range of 844.06 to 1096.50.

## Financial commentary

Revenue has risen each year, from $226.95B in fiscal 2022 to $242.29B in 2023, $254.45B in 2024 and $275.24B in 2025. Net income followed the same path, moving from $5.84B to $6.29B, then $7.37B, and reaching $8.10B in fiscal 2025. Net margin is 3.0%, a thin figure typical of a high-volume warehouse model, and revenue growth is shown at 11.1%. Return on equity is 28.4%, and debt to equity is a modest 0.24. The dividend yield is 0.6%. Recent news reported fourth-quarter sales up 11.2% to $93.9B, consistent with this growth picture.

## Comps commentary

The primary comparison is forward P/E, where Costco trades at 36.8 against a peer median of 16.3, a premium of 125%. Trailing P/E of 44.5 is 120% above the peer median of 20.2. On enterprise value, EV/EBITDA of 27.5 is 144% above the median of 11.3, and EV/Revenue of 1.3 is 66% above 0.8. Operating metrics help explain part of the gap: revenue growth of 11.1% is 109% above the peer median of 5.3%, and leverage is 81% lower, with debt to equity of 0.24 against 1.26. Net margin of 3.0% is in line with the peer median, only 1% higher. Among individual peers, Walmart sits closest on valuation with a forward P/E of 32.3, while the rest of the group is far lower. The comparison shows a company priced well above its peers on nearly every multiple.

## Risk commentary

The most severe risks, each rated 3, are heavy reliance on U.S. and Canadian operations, the possibility that membership growth and loyalty may falter, and intense competition from other retailers and warehouse clubs. Because earnings depend so much on North American results and on retaining members, weakness in either area could hurt results. At moderate severity of 2, the filing cites domestic and international economic weakness, supplier failures on quality, timing or price, and the chance that expansion into existing and new markets or acquisitions may not succeed. The recent nationwide partnership with DoorDash relates loosely to the competition and growth themes, though the filing risks do not address it directly.
